headline: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of ‘incitement,’ handed 4-year sentence
author: Rael Ombuor

paragraphs.text: Tanzania’s main opposition leader, Tundu Lissu, 58, has been sentenced to serve four years in prison for “incitement,” over a statement he made in the run-up to last year’s election. He was acquitted of a treason charge.
Rights groups have accused the Tanzanian government of using trumped up charges to threaten, silence and imprison critics.

Lissu’s opposition party was shut out of the election after authorities accused it of promoting a boycott. The party, Chadema, of which Lissu is chair, had demanded electoral reforms, mounting a campaign it called “No Reforms, No Election.”
He was arrested and charged with treason, for which he could have faced the death penalty. The 18-month court case has drawn international scrutiny and criticism.
While the high court in Dar es Salaam acquitted him on the treason charge Friday, it found him guilty of incitement for statements alleged to have undermined the election.

After the vote, Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan presided over a widely documented crackdown on dissent, which descended into violence. Activists say state security forces killed more than 1,000 people, a charge the government denies.

In a statement posted to social media, Lissu condemned the treason charges as a “political fabrication,” a view he said the court had affirmed in his acquittal. He condemned his conviction for incitement.
“This is not justice. This is damage control,” the statement said. “History will record how the court searched for a lesser charge simply to keep me in prison.”
Hassan has not offered public comment on the verdict.
Lissu survived an assassination attempt in 2017, in which he was shot 16 times. At that time, John Pombe Magufuli was president and Hassan was vice president. No one was convicted for the attack.
